newsitem.title: USA: Hutchinson sees suspension shipments drop.
newsitem.headline: Hutchinson sees suspension shipments drop.

text.p: Hutchinson Technology Inc said Monday it expects fiscal 1997 fourth quarter shipments of conventional suspensions to be down about five percent.
It added that the continued ramp-up of its TSA suspensions also will reduce gross margins from the prior quarter level.

Earlier, Hutchinson, which supplies suspension assemblies for computer disk drives, reported fiscal third quarter earnings of $0.68 a share, compared with $0.31 a year ago. Sales rose to $121.7 million from $91.4 million a year ago.

"In the fiscal 1997 third quarter, we shipped 195 million suspensions compared to 145 million in the fiscal 1996 third quarter, reflecting the increased demand for our products and the capacity we have added to accommodate customer requirements," Wayne Fortun, president, said in a statement.
He added the gross profit margin rose to 27 percent in the third quarter from 24 percent a year ago.
Fortun said the company continues to add manufacturing capacity to support long-term demand trends.

"Over the long term, demand for disk storage continues to grow thanks to the increasingly widespread use of computers and network file servers, the proliferation of storage-intensive applications and the emergence of non-computer applications, such as voice and video storage," he added.
Fortun said Hutchinson's expansion will help its production of TSA suspensions, which incorporate integrated electrical leads.

"As we continue to implement solutions for various start-up problems for these products, our output in recent weeks has exceeded 400,000 units per week," Fortun said. "Currently, we expect to be able to produce more than two million TSA suspensions per week during the first quarter of fiscal 1998."

He added that TSA suspensions are under evaluation in three new drive programs, have been designed-in on a total of 12 programs at five major disk drive manufacturers and are in use on one customer disk drive program currently in production.
